response.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY films DESC, original_language_id IS NULL, original_language_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The schema is MySQL (Sakila), so GROUP BY places all NULL original_language_id films in one group, and the query uses MySQL syntax.
'At least 20.99' is an inclusive filter (replacement_cost >= 20.99), applied before grouping.

'Any missing counts last' is read as a tie-breaker: when group sizes are equal, the NULL-language group comes after the named-language groups. Missing values are never counted as a sort key on their own.
The average uses rental_rate / rental_duration per film. Both columns are NOT NULL, so no rows are dropped by the average, and rental_duration is at least 3, so there is no division by zero.

alternatives.interpretation: 'Any missing counts last' means the NULL-language group always goes last, even if it has more films than other groups. Sort by the missing flag first, then by film count descending.
